taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes Recuero et al. (2006) split P. regilla into three species (regilla, sierra, hypochondriaca) that other nuclear data did not support; NatureServe records list the synonym Hyliola regilla, and Montana Field Guide says Montana animals once called Pacific treefrog are the Sierran treefrog.
fieldMarks: Small, up to about 5 cm snout-vent length; colour highly variable (usually green or brown; also gray, tan, bronze, blackish or reddish) with irregular dark spots.
Dark stripe from the snout to the shoulder; toe tips expanded.
Mature males have a dark throat; breeding call is a loud repeated 'kreck-ek'.
Tadpoles brown or olive, eyes widely spaced at the margin of the head when seen from above, up to about 44 mm.
behavior: Breeding mostly winter or spring, sometimes summer; calling often happens outside the breeding season and far from breeding sites.
Eggs in soft loose clumps of about 10-80, in shallow water; larvae metamorphose in about 2-3 months.
After breeding they bask on leaves of broad-leaved shrubs far from water and sometimes climb into trees; migrate up to several hundred metres between breeding and upland sites.
Eats beetles, flies, spiders, ants and isopods; inactive in freezing weather and extreme drought.
habitat: Grassland, shrubland, woodland, forest and farmland; on land except in the breeding season.
Breeds in shallow marshes, lakes, ponds, ditches, reservoirs and slow streams.
range: Southern British Columbia south through the western United States to southern Baja California, east to Montana, Idaho and Nevada; introduced populations on Haida Gwaii (Queen Charlotte Islands) and Revillagigedo Island, Alaska, and probably in desert California and Arizona. Montana populations are now attributed to the Sierran treefrog.

lookalikes.name: Sierran treefrog
lookalikes.howToTell: Not separable by appearance; genetics and range distinguish them (Montana Field Guide).
